text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, currently on a three-day visit to Slovakia, is expected to sign an agreement on cooperation between the Russian and Slovak central banks.
- A special committee in charge of organising the forthcoming referenda on NATO membership and direct presidential elecions said people will vote on one ballot in the two plebiscites.

- The state-run postal monopoly Slovenska Posta (SP) said it posted a loss of 11,700 crowns for the first quarter but that it expected to return to profitability this year due to a recently approved increase in postal prices. SP said its revenues should total some 3.9 billion crowns this year.

- A policeman was killed in a car blast on Monday, bringing the number of law enforcement agents this month to three. Police said attacks against policemen meant an open war against them and society as a whole.

SME - The Slovak government argued to the Constitutional Court that the constitution cannot be changed by a referendum, The government was reacting to opposition attempts to create direct presidential elections through a plebiscite.

- Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) leader Jan Carnogursky said slower deliveries of equipment enabling compatibility of the air force with NATO systems may endanger Slovakia's participation in NATO training manouevres scheduled to take plave in Norway next May.
- Opposition parties said they would work out a draft law to prevent the planned privatisation of the second terrestrial channel of the public Slovak Television (STV).
- Prime Minister Vladmir Meciar said the Czech Republic must return Slovakia's part of the former Czechoslovakia's gold reserves to restore Slovak confidence in Prague.
PRAVDA - Slovakia is expected to obtain a Russin air defence system S-300 PMU-1 as a part of repayment of Russia's debt to Slovakia.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Economics Ministry has yet to define commodities which will be affected by a recently adopted import deposit measure.
- Some 240,387 orders to sell privatisation bonds are on the market, but there is no demand for the paper at the minimum guaranteed price of 8,160 crowns.
